scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by making that Facebook post about my best friend's trip to India. Let me start by going through the situation again to make sure I understand everything. My best friend, who's 21, went on a three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive! Plus, he paid for the entire trip himself, which cost over $3000. That's a lot of money, so I can imagine he must have saved up or worked hard to afford it. Now, he's a pretty shy and quiet guy. I know he didn't tell many people about the trip before he left, and I'm not sure if he was planning to tell anyone when he got back. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he did, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to let all his friends and family know about the trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn't want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he's such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post, and I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing by making that Facebook post? Is it AITA (Ask If It's Too Awkward) for making that post? First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is a term used on the internet, often in forums like Reddit, where people ask if something they did is too awkward or inappropriate. It's a way to get advice from others on whether they handled a situation well or not. In this case, I made a Facebook post about my friend's volunteer trip without asking him first. He ended up being upset about it, saying he didn't want the attention and that I shouldn't have done it without his consent. So, to determine if it's AITA, I need to consider a few things: 1. **Respect for Privacy**: Did I respect my friend's privacy by posting about his trip without his knowledge? 2. **Intentions**: Were my intentions good? I thought I was doing something nice by giving him recognition. 3. **Impact on the Relationship**: Did this action affect our friendship negatively? 4. **Communication**: Did I communicate with him about making the post before doing it? 5. **His Feelings**: Did I consider how he might feel about the post? Let me go through each of these points. 1. **Respect for Privacy**: My friend is shy and didn't tell many people about the trip. By posting about it on Facebook, I might have invaded his privacy, especially since he didn't want to share it with others. He might have wanted to keep his trip private or only share it in his own way and on his own terms. 2. **Intentions**: My intention was to give him recognition for his good work. I thought it was a nice thing to do because he's shy and wouldn't tell people himself. However, good intentions don't always mean the action is appropriate or respectful. 3. **Impact on the Relationship**: After the post, he seemed annoyed at me, didn't want to hang out, and was upset when I texted him. This definitely had a negative impact on our relationship. It created tension and made him feel uncomfortable. 4. **Communication**: I didn't communicate with him about making the post before doing it. I assumed he would be okay with it because I thought it was a good thing. However, not discussing it with him first was a mistake. 5. **His Feelings**: I didn't consider how he might feel about the post. He made it clear that he didn't want attention for his trip and that he went for self-improvement, not to brag or get recognition. By posting about it, I might have made him feel uncomfortable or self-conscious. Considering all these points, it seems like making the Facebook post without his consent was not appropriate. It disrespected his privacy, didn't consider his feelings, and negatively impacted our relationship. Even though my intentions were good, the way I went about it was not respectful or considerate of his wishes. Therefore, it is AITA for making that post.
